title: Carbonara
notes: Pick the eggs with the darkest yolks; colour comes from the hen's feed.
If using a whole piece of guanciale: cut off the rind, slice 1 cm thick, then into batons 1 × 1 × 4 cm. Pat pre-cut cubes very dry before rendering.
If the cream comes out grainy, use 60 °C next time; if it stays thin, 70 °C.

steps.text: Fill the TM7 bowl with {pecorino} and {parmigiano}. Blend, then scrape down the sides. TM7: 10 sec / speed 10
Put in the yolks of {eggs}. Mix to a paste and leave it in the bowl. TM7: 20 sec / speed 4
Bring a large pot of water to the boil with 7 g salt per litre.
Meanwhile, put {guanciale} in a cold wide pan in a single layer, no oil. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring once or twice, until the fat pools and the pieces turn translucent.
Drop {spaghetti} into the boiling water. Cook 1 min less than the packet time.
Meanwhile, raise the pan to medium-high. Leave the pieces mostly alone until deep golden and crackling.
Lift the pieces onto a plate with a slotted spoon, then take the pan off the heat. Add {pepper-fat}, then wait 20 seconds.
Once the pasta has cooked 3 min, ladle {pasta-water-cream} into the TM7 bowl and pour in the fat with its pepper. Cook until thick, smooth and glossy, like a custard. TM7: 5 min / 65 °C / speed 3
Scoop out {pasta-water-toss} and set it aside. Drain the pasta and return it to the empty pot, off the heat.
Pour the cream over and toss hard. Add the reserved water a splash at a time until every strand is coated and glossy.
Plate immediately. Top with the guanciale, then {pepper-top}.
